newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics beats estimates, shares up.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics beats estimates, shares up.

text.p: Computer workstation maker Silicon Graphics Inc. posted a strong gain in fiscal fourth quarter income Thursday, startling Wall Street after nearly two years of quarterly shortfalls.
The company said it earned $102 million, or 56 cents a share, on sales of $1.2 billion. A year earlier, the company lost $48.7 million, or 30 cents a share, on sales of $977 million.

The company, whose products are used in computer-intensive applications from complex weather modeling to special effects in movies, said revenue growth was balanced across all its business units and was driven especially by the success of its Octane workstation and Origin 2000 scalable server families.

Its profit, which was announced after the close of market trading, exceeded the 34 cents a share that Wall Street analysts surveyed by First Call had expected. In after-hours trading, its stock jumped to $23 a share from $19.44.

The favorable earnings report gave Silicon Graphics investors a welcome boost after a sweeping product transition over the last year battered their shares and contributed to repeated earnings disappointments.
"This quarter was all about execution," Chief Executive Officer Edward McCracken said in a statement.

"Our product transition is complete, we are shipping our entire product line without significant constraints and, most importantly, the new products are finding strong acceptance with customers," he said.
Analysts said investors were still likely to be wary of the stock after so many quarters of having missed its projected results.

"Silicon Graphics is a low-expectation stock," said David Wu, an analyst at ABN AMRO Chicago Corp. "For seven consecutive quarters they haven't made their numbers. This time they more than made their numbers."
Wu said Wall Street had been expecting revenues in the $1 billion range.

The fourth-quarter result included pre-tax merger charges of $6 million related to the company's April 1996 acquisition of supercomputer maker Cray Research. That compared with charges of $120 million in the same quarter a year earlier related to the same transaction.
A spokesman for Silicon Graphics said the fourth quarter was the last in which the company was expecting to report charges related to the Cray acquisition.
For the year, Silicon Graphics earned $78.5 million, or 43 cents a share, on sales of $3.09 billion. A year earlier, the company earned $115 million, or 65 cents a share, on sales of $2.55 billion.
